history.content: Hi, my phone has no service at all—no bars, nothing loads, and I can't send picture messages. It's completely dead as far as the network goes.

I can help you troubleshoot this issue. To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide one of the following:

- The phone number associated with your account
- Your customer ID
- Your full name and date of birth

Once I have this information, I can check your line status and assist you further.
My phone number is +1-617-555-0148 and my name is Sofia Martinez.

Thank you for the information. Your line status is currently Active, which means there are no suspensions or contract issues on your account.

Let’s proceed with troubleshooting your phone’s network connection. I’ll guide you through a few steps to help identify the cause of the “no service” issue. Are you able to interact with your phone right now to perform some quick checks?
Yes, I have my phone with me and can follow your instructions.

Great! Let’s start by checking your phone’s status bar for any indicators that might explain the lack of service.

Please use the function or setting on your phone to check the status bar and let me know what you see, especially regarding:

- Airplane mode (is it on?)
- Signal bars (any bars or “no signal” icon?)
- Network type (e.g., 5G, 4G, etc.)
- Any other unusual icons

If you’re not sure how to check, let me know what you see at the top of your screen, or if you have a “status” or “network” section in your phone’s settings.
I see Airplane Mode is on, and there’s a 'No Signal' icon in the status bar. Data is enabled and battery is at 87%.

That explains the issue—when Airplane Mode is on, all wireless connections (including cellular service) are disabled, which is why you have no signal and nothing loads.

Please turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. You can usually do this by:

- Swiping down from the top of your screen to open the quick settings panel.
- Tapping the airplane icon to turn it off.

Once you’ve turned off Airplane Mode, wait a few seconds and check if your signal bars return and if you can use your phone normally. Let me know what happens after you do this.
Airplane mode is now OFF. The 'No Signal' icon is gone, but I still have no signal bars and nothing is loading on my phone.

Thank you for turning off Airplane Mode. Since you still have no signal bars, let’s check if your SIM card is being detected correctly, as SIM issues can also cause a complete loss of service.

Please check your SIM card status on your phone. If you have a SIM status or network settings section, look for any messages about the SIM card (such as “No SIM,” “SIM not detected,” or “SIM locked”). 

If you’re able to, please let me know what your phone says about the SIM card status. If you’re unsure how to check, I can guide you through the process.
My phone says the SIM status is active.

Thank you for confirming that your SIM status is active. That means your SIM card is detected and not locked.

Next, let’s check your phone’s network settings, specifically the Access Point Name (APN) settings, as incorrect APN settings can prevent your phone from connecting to the network.

Please check your APN settings and let me know if you see anything unusual, such as missing or incorrect information, or if there’s an option to reset to default. If you’re unsure how to check, I can guide you through the steps.
I checked my APN settings. The APN name is 'fast.telecom.net', but the status says 'Not set'. The MMSC URL is listed as 'http://mms.telecom.net/mms/wapenc'.

Thank you for checking your APN settings. The APN name being “Not set” is unusual and could be the reason you’re not getting service. Let’s reset your APN settings to the default values to resolve any configuration issues.

Please reset your APN settings to default on your phone. After resetting, you’ll need to reboot your device for the changes to take effect.

Here’s what to do:
1. Reset your APN settings to default.
2. Restart (reboot) your phone.

Once your phone has restarted, check if you have signal bars and if your service is restored. Let me know the results after you complete these steps.
I reset the APN settings to default and rebooted my phone. The status says the changes were applied, but I still have no signal bars and nothing is loading.

Thank you for following those steps. Since your SIM is active, Airplane Mode is off, and APN settings are now default, but you still have no signal bars or service, let’s check one more thing: your network mode preference.

Sometimes, if your phone is set to use an unsupported network mode (like 2G or 3G only), it may not connect properly. Please check your phone’s network mode preference and let me know what it is currently set to (e.g., 5G, 4G, 3G, 2G, or “auto”). If it’s set to 2G or 3G, try changing it to “4G/5G preferred” or “auto” if available.

Let me know what your current network mode is, or if you need help finding this setting.
My network mode was set to 'auto' and includes 5G, 4G, and 3G. I did not see an option for 2G only, and it's already on the preferred setting.

Thank you for confirming your network mode is set to “auto” with 5G, 4G, and 3G included. Since you’ve already checked Airplane Mode, SIM status, APN settings, and network mode, and your line is active with no suspensions, you’ve completed all standard troubleshooting steps.

At this point, the issue may be related to a deeper technical problem with your line, device, or network provisioning that requires advanced support.

I will transfer you to a human agent who can investigate this further and resolve your issue.

YOU ARE BEING TRANSFERRED TO A HUMAN AGENT. PLEASE HOLD ON.
